quick_read.weather_md: **Weather:** 29°C high / 21°C low. Humid, *tsuyu* (rainy season) is happening, babe. Showers in 30–60 min bursts, not all-day misery. Some hours dry, some hours not. You're fine if you don't pack like it's California.
quick_read.uv_md: **UV:** Sneaky 7–9 between showers. Cloudy ≠ safe. **SPF 30+ broad spectrum** every morning, re-up after lunch if you've been outside. Cap or umbrella does double duty here — sun AND rain. Your skin will thank you.
quick_read.uv_advisory_md: *📎 Goose Investigation Bureau — sourcing UV from EPA + Cancer Research UK. UV 1–2 = no protection needed. UV 3+ = sunscreen + shade + hat + sunglasses. UV 8+ = limit midday sun. UV 11+ = stay out of midday sun entirely.*
quick_read.budget_hint_md: **Daily budget — $140 average.** With my picks below, that's real. Save: trains instead of cabs, konbini lunch instead of sit-down. Splurge: omakase pushes you toward $300. **Bonus:** *tsuyu* = lowest hotel prices of any non-winter month. You're catching it cheap.
quick_read.intro_md: > *Babe, I dug through your week, pulled what's actually happening, found you the spots locals love, lined it all up. The full goose investigation is below. I went HARD. You're so set.*
quick_read.do_now_md:
**Do now:**
- **Load Suica or PASMO into Apple Wallet before you land.** No physical card needed — just tap your phone at the gates and ride. Heads-up: JR (that's the main train company, they run the famous green Yamanote loop) raised fares for the first time in nearly 40 years back in March. You're still paying like $2-3 per ride, just don't trust the old prices your friend quoted from last summer.
- **Book SKY-HI at Budokan Jun 18** if a sacred-venue J-pop/hip-hop night sounds right. Ticketing through e+ (eplus) or PIA — going fast.
- **Cash, babe. Pull ¥30,000 (~$200) day one.** 7-Eleven ATMs accept foreign cards 24/7. Small ramen shops, shrines, festivals = cash-only. Cards work in Shinjuku/Ginza but stop the moment you wander off the main drag.
quick_read.restaurant_hook_md: **The Places to Eat list below is the play.** Michelin Guide picks, mostly NOT starred, which is the whole point. Some are walk-ins, all are spots locals fight to keep quiet. Book Den + Tempura Kondo 60 days out if you want them. Trust me trust me, lock it now.

happening.news_md:
- **Tsuyu (rainy season) active Jun 7 – Jul 19.** Tokyo gets ~12 rainy days in June, but rain is patchy — 30 to 60-min bursts, not all-day washouts. Underground shopping in Shinjuku + Shibuya, JR's covered station network, you can dodge most of it. Hotel rates lowest of any non-winter month. [src 1]
- **JR train fare hike — 7.1% from March 2026.** First blanket increase in nearly 40 years. Affects every JR line including Yamanote, Chuo, Sobu. Still the cheapest way to ride; tourist 24h/48h passes still good value. [src 2]
- **Takanawa Gateway City opened March 27, 2026.** Brand-new district in Shinagawa — hotels, offices, international convention center, futuristic JR station with patrol robots and Vtuber customer-service screens. Real cyberpunk Tokyo if you want to see it. Free walk-through. [src 2]
happening.sports_md: - **⚾ NPB baseball — Giants at Tokyo Dome, Swallows at Jingu Stadium.** Check `npb.jp` the week of your trip for the home schedule. The Tokyo Dome experience hits different than US baseball — choreographed chants, *uriko* beer girls running stadium stairs with kegs strapped to their backs, fan towels for every player. Worth a night even if you don't follow the league, babe. I'm being serious. [src 3, 4]
happening.entertainment_md:
- **🎤 SKY-HI at Nippon Budokan — Jun 18, 7pm.** Already flagged. The Budokan is *the* venue — Beatles, Cheap Trick, every legendary live album was recorded there. Even if you don't know SKY-HI's music, the venue itself is the experience. [src 5]
- **🎭 Sanno Festival — Jun 7–17, runs every 2 years (2026 is on!).** One of Tokyo's three Great Festivals at Hie Shrine, portable mikoshi parades through Akasaka. Catches the tail of your arrival window. [src 6]
- **🌸 Bunkyo Hydrangea Festival at Hakusan Shrine — peak mid-June.** ~3,000 hydrangea plants in full bloom. Free, packed weekends, calm weekday mornings. The blue-purple ones, babe. Aesthetic. [src 6]
- **⛩️ Torikoe Festival near Asakusa — mid-June annual.** Mikoshi parade in old downtown. Crowded, joyful, very photogenic. [src 6]

brief.watch_md:
- **teamLab Planets (Toyosu) — ¥3,800 (~$25).** Immersive digital art, wet floors. Wear shorts or roll your pants — they WILL ask you. Photo: mirror koi room (queue ready).
- **Yanaka — old-Tokyo walk + cat-spotting — FREE.** Niche pick, babe, I cannot stress this enough. Yanaka survived the 1945 firebombing, so the wooden buildings are real-real old. Stone-paved alleys, hand-carved seal shops, and cats EVERYWHERE — Yanaka is famous for them. Quiet weekday mornings. Photo: "Yuyake Dandan," the sunset stair at the entrance to Yanaka Ginza.
- **Shibuya Sky — sunset slot — ¥3,000 (~$20).** Open-air rooftop, full Tokyo panorama, the Scramble crossing below looking tiny. Book the 4:30–5:30pm window. Photo: south-facing helipad looking toward Tokyo Tower.
- **Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building observatory — FREE.** People pay ¥3,000+ for Skytree. This one is free. Two observation decks, North + South. North closes for a lights show some evenings; check before going. Insider hack.
- **Tsukiji Outer Market — mornings only — FREE entry, food $2-15 per item.** Inner wholesale moved to Toyosu but the outer market is alive. Tamagoyaki on a stick, uni samples, knife shops. Photo: knife-sharpening demo at Aritsugu.
brief.eat_md:
*Most are Guide-listed, not starred. Real food, no gold-card spectacle.*

- **Den** — Two stars. Playful kaiseki, the KFC-style fried-chicken course is famous. Book 60 days out via Pocket Concierge. *(~$280 pp tasting menu)*
- **Nakiryu** — Bib Gourmand. Tantan-men ramen that earned a Michelin nod. Line by 11am or accept a 90-minute wait. *(~$13 a bowl)*
- **Tonkatsu Aoki** — Guide listed. Pork-cutlet temple, counter only. Walk-in but go off-peak (2pm). *(~$25-35)*
- **Tempura Kondo** — Two stars. Counter-only tempura, masterclass-level. Phone reservation only, usually through your hotel concierge. *(~$180 pp lunch, $280 dinner)*
- **Sushi Saito** — Three stars. Near-impossible booking, hotel concierge or existing-customer referral only. Filed under "if you somehow get in, do it." *(~$450 pp omakase)*
brief.knowing_md:
- **Trains are quiet. No phone calls, no speakerphone, no loud conversations.** Locals visibly tense when foreigners break this. Texting fine. Music with earphones fine. Voice calls = social violation.
- **Cash is still real.** Cards accepted in Shinjuku, Ginza, big chains. Off-the-main-drag = cash only. 7-Eleven ATMs take foreign cards 24/7.
- **Tipping is not done. Don't.** It confuses servers, sometimes insults them. Service is included. Saying "*gochisousama deshita*" (thank you for the meal) on the way out is the real tip.
- **Trash cans are rare.** Carry a small plastic bag for wrappers and bottles until you find a konbini bin. Tokyo is *immaculate* and that's how.
- **Convenience stores (konbini) are food.** 7-Eleven, Lawson, FamilyMart — actual real meals, $5 dinners, egg sandwiches that taste like clouds. Babe, do not skip the konbini experience.

budget_usd.notes: Mid = business hotel ($90), 2 meals incl. ramen + izakaya ($35), train day-pass + 1 paid attraction ($25). Sushi tasting menus push high tier fast.
